items.excerpt: Solo developer Thales Pereira has released StemDeck, a free open-source stem separation tool for Windows, macOS and Linux that runs entirely locally. He built it to help his kid practice drums, without a subscription or uploading music to someone else's server.

An argument that musicians have been asking the wrong question about AI: instead of fighting models trained on everyone's catalogue, train a private model on your own back catalogue and treat it as a personal collaborator. A practical how-to framing for artist-owned models.

Social remix and mashup platform Hook has finalised a 'landmark' licensing agreement with Universal Music Group, letting fans legally rework major-label tracks in-app. Rightsholders and artists get credited and paid on the derivative works.

A hands-on tutorial on salvaging vocal samples ripped from the internet or vinyl using LALAL.AI's new Lynx separation algorithm, then treating the artefacts so the acapella sits in a track. Craft-level detail on where AI separation still needs a human ear.

AI-assisted plugin development is redefining how music software gets made, and by whom. Developers describe shipping DSP tools without a traditional coding background — and what that flood does to plugin quality and the market.

Suno Studio 2.0 puts a chat-driven AI assistant inside its browser DAW: you can talk to the session like a collaborator, plus new MIDI editing, advanced stem separation and automation curves. Generative music moves from prompt box to production environment.

MusicRadar's read on Suno Studio 2.0: the chatbot can control your project, transform sounds and even generate custom plugins on demand inside the DAW. A DAW where the effects chain itself is prompted into existence.

MIDI support, a chat bar and custom plugin generation land in Suno's browser-based DAW, with no download restrictions in Studio. gearnews walks through what the second generation actually changes for producers exporting into a real session.

AM I AUDIO's I AM CHOIR turns a single sung take into a full choir part that follows your lyrics, melody, phrasing and timing — processed locally, no cloud round-trip. A neural vocal instrument aimed squarely at arrangement work.

Apex Plugins has released Apex Amp, a virtual guitar workstation with 8-stage tube preamp modelling, reactive power-amp sag and an AI preset assistant that dials in a tone from a description. Windows VST3 and standalone at a $49 intro price.

Beatport has banned fully AI-generated tracks while still allowing AI-assisted ones, tagged at upload. CEO: "There is a difference between a tool that assists human creation and a system that replaces it entirely."
Beatport is now blocking fully AI-generated uploads using a new detection tool, with AI-assisted tracks permitted but labelled. The producer-facing view of what actually gets flagged at ingestion.
Beatport is banning fully AI-generated music and rolling out the Beatdapp detection tool to enforce it, effective immediately. Its own survey says 77% of DJs want music from real artists.
Synthtopia's early report on Beatport's policy shift against AI-generated music, and where the line falls between an AI tool in the chain and an AI-made record.
Spotify will badge AI-generated artist profiles as 'AI Personas' and, by default, keep them out of editorial and algorithmic recommendations. Disclosure now directly determines discovery.

Rolling Stone details Spotify's plan to label AI artists, with self-disclosure opening 11 August and the policy taking effect in mid-September. Music from badged profiles is excluded from editorial and algorithmic surfaces.

Five things to know about Suno's BMG alliance: opt-in artist participation, hard download caps by tier, audio watermarking and fingerprinting, and what it signals about the licensed model due later in 2026.

BMG and Suno's licensing deal covers recorded and publishing works for derivative creation, with artists and songwriters required to opt in before their music can be used — and compensated when they do.
Suno's BMG deal deepens generative AI's ties to the majors ahead of its first industry-built model, alongside watermarking, fingerprinting and new download limits to curb streaming fraud.
UMG has partnered with Hook to license fan-created remixes and mashups across social platforms, turning derivative fan edits into a tracked, payable format instead of takedown fodder.

Tyga openly admits using Suno to make his latest album — raising the question of whether the new AI chart-eligibility rules would disqualify it. A first real test case for disclosure norms at the top of the market.

A first-person account of using AI to finally hear lyrics that sat in a notebook for thirty years — and what happened after the novelty wore off. A grounded look at generative tools as a route into craft rather than a replacement for it.

Spotify says it has removed 75 million AI-generated spam tracks, alongside new impersonation and disclosure rules. Scale numbers that reframe what 'discovery' means for human artists sharing the same shelf.

Organismi OR—1 is an artful, breathing stochastic MIDI pattern generator — free for iPad as an AUv3, €19.99 on macOS. A reminder that algorithmic composition can feel organic rather than machine-made.
